title: Ask entropy mapping and probe scenarios — June 2025
content:
Purpose
This is a lightweight, experimental synthesis of recent customer asks where the signal has high entropy (many variants, unclear root need). Goal: map the variation, propose low-effort probes to reduce uncertainty, and pick the top 3 candidate features to run validation with product/eng.

Context / why this doc now
- Multiple enterprise customers surfaced similar friction types in the last quarter but with different surface language: ‘token cost spikes’, ‘inconsistent latency by route’, ‘unexpected fallback to smaller models’, ‘confusing rollouts’.
- Customer Success (field) wants a concise set of experiments we can run in 2–4 sprints that will: (a) reduce support noise, (b) surface quantitative checks we can add to Console, and (c) produce a clear implementation decision.

Quick summary of signals observed
- Signal A: Cost/latency: 42 mentions across accounts (high variance). Common phrases: “token blow-ups”, “spiky invoices”, “embeddings cost different than text”.
- Signal B: Rollouts & model variants: 26 mentions. Pain: canary falls back and client sees degraded output unexpectedly.
- Signal C: Debugging surface: 33 mentions. Requests: better per-request trace, sample inputs preserved, and a unified ‘why-this-model’ explanation.

Entropy mapping (rough)
- Method: took 240 raw support notes + Vega exports of usage logs for 8 customers; clustered by phrase-level edit-distance, manually tagged. Entropy = number of distinct phrasings / total mentions per problem lane.
- Findings: Cost/latency lane has highest phrase diversity (tokenization, batching, price vs quality trade-offs), suggesting customers conflate UI terminology with technical behavior.

Representative customer quotes (preserve raw flavor)
- “We used to get steady bills — last month it spiked 3x for one endpoint — no explanation.” — mid-market fintech
- “Canaries switched on and suddenly our NLU regressed. We had to rollback manually — can we auto-fallback?” — enterprise retail AI team
- “I can’t tell which call used my cached prefix — need a sample hash or id.” — startup, data-sensitive

Priority probe candidates (intent: low dev cost, high info value)
1) Billing-Delta Snackbar (probe): a small Console UI + email digest that shows week-over-week token breakdowns by route, color-coded by model variant and caching hit/miss.
   - Hypothesis: visibility reduces support tickets and reveals whether requests are truly expensive or misattributed.
   - Success metric: 30% drop in billing-related tickets from pilot accounts in 4 weeks.
   - Engineering estimate: 1 backend endpoint + 1 small Console page + email job (3 dev-weeks).

2) Canary Health Tagging (probe): attach lightweight metadata to canary responses (model-variant, policy, trace-id) surfaced in Console and optionally in webhook payloads so customers can detect unexpected fallback.
   - Hypothesis: surface-level tags reduce time-to-detect and root-cause for regressions.
   - Success metric: mean time to rollback reduced by 40% in pilot.
   - Engineering estimate: 2–3 dev-weeks (runtime change + Console display).

3) Sample-Preservation Toggle (probe): opt-in route-level setting to persist n sample inputs + outputs for 7 days (encrypted), visible to customer with one-click export for debugging.
   - Hypothesis: having ground-truth examples will make debug cycles faster and reduce back-and-forths.
   - Privacy note: default off; needs legal review for enterprise.
   - Engineering estimate: 3–4 dev-weeks + security gating.

Decision matrix (fast view)
- Cost vs Effort vs Impact: Billing-Delta (low effort, high impact), Canary Health Tagging (medium effort, high impact), Sample Preservation (higher effort, mid impact due to privacy review).

Proposed rollout plan (pilot-first)
- Week 0: pick 3 pilot customers (A, B, C) representing different tiers (startup, mid-market, enterprise). CS owners: Leo (A), Ava (B), Samir (C).
- Week 1–2: instrument billing-delta and canary health tagging only. Collect logs and initial UX feedback.
- Week 3–4: evaluate metrics; if billing probe shows >25% ticket reduction, expand to 10 pilots and schedule product review for prioritizing persistent feature work.

Operational notes / things to watch
- Data retention and privacy: Sample preservation needs specific policy and contract language; engage Legal early.
- Metric leaks: ensure Console email digest doesn’t surface raw customer PII.
- Observability: create a temp dashboard (SLO-ish) for pilot KPIs: ticket count, mean time to detect, billing variance.

Open questions / unresolved threads
- Which exact tokenization breakdown is most actionable? per-token type or per-segment? (ENG-4821 linked for initial sampling logic).
- Can runtime emit health tags without a measurable CPU/latency penalty? Need an engineering spike to confirm.
- Do we want automatic rollback suggestions or leave that manual? Product decision to make after pilot.

Owner & next actions (short list)
- Maya: circle back with Product to confirm prioritization slot and legal review request. Due: 2025-06-19.
- Leo: recruit pilot customers and draft pilot onboarding email (template). Due: 2025-06-18.
- Ava & Samir: confirm telemetry requirements with Eng-SRE and estimate the spike work. Due: 2025-06-21.

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep probes intentionally narrow — we want signal, not shipping full features yet.
- Capture one example flow per pilot customer (annotated timeline) — will help in product review.
